Adding the routing/ops detail here so it can be copy/pasted into the narrative:

Summary (technical):
- Tenant isolation is enforced at multiple layers: network namespace + overlay (VPC per-tenant / per-customer VLAN segments on Dedicated pools), hypervisor-level process isolation, and model-serving runtime sandboxing (process-level cgroups + seccomp).
- For Dedicated: customer-dedicated GPU pools are placed in isolated VPCs with dedicated subnets and NAT gateways. Inter-subnet routing is blocked by default; explicit route tables and security groups are used for operator-run management planes.
- For Private (VPC-hosted / on-prem): we provide a private control plane proxy that is reachable only over configured peering/VPN. KMS keys are customer-managed or stored in a customer KMS project; we publish key IDs in the segmentation matrix.
- Egress fencing: default deny; only approved egress to telemetry endpoints is allowed (and logged). We run periodic egress rule audits (automated), and any emergency exception is recorded in Jira and subject to postmortem review.
- Verification hooks: daily config snapshotting, weekly compliance diff reports, drift alerts to PagerDuty when sensitive groups change, and quarterly tabletop exercises for failover and isolation breach scenarios.

Let me know if you want more depth on router ACLs or BGP/peering specifics — I kept it intentionally high level for the initial narrative.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex —

Attached are the deliverables requested:

1) isolation-narrative-v1.pdf — 2-page narrative describing logical and operational controls across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
2) vpc-segmentation-diagram.png — simplified diagram showing Dedicated VPC per-customer, control plane peering, and Private on-prem routing options.
3) segmentation-matrix-202609.pdf — mapping of SIG/CAIQ controls -> evidence artifact (logs, config dumps, screenshots, Drive links).

High-level notes:
- Hosted: multi-tenant runtime with strict prefix/KV caching boundaries, logical tenant isolation via namespaces, and strict RBAC for the control plane. We include sample logs and tenant id scoping in the matrix.
- Dedicated: physical isolation at the GPU pool + VPC isolation; we call out reserved IP ranges and NAT boundary controls in the matrix.
- Private: customer-managed network, optional air-gapped package; we provide KMS integration guidance and a checklist for on-prem hardening.

Operational checkpoints (short):
- Weekly automated config snapshot + drift diff (retained 90 days)
- Egress audits and exported reports (retained 180 days)
- KMS access review (monthly) and key rotation notes in the matrix
- Change approvals via PR + change ticket; emergency changes documented in Jira SUP-xxxx with postmortem link.

Next steps: please confirm if the level of detail is sufficient for your SIG entry; if you need additional artifacts (full CAIQ, CAIQ-attached evidence binder, or SOC 2 mapping) we can package and deliver that within two business days.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference
